adoption_basis.note: Variant C is established for the bounded candidate layer through the authenticated subjective-UAT path. That acceptance is not authority for record_human_disposition and does not satisfy, close or answer any RC28 finding.

event_id.algorithm: sha256 over the canonical JSON of the closed field inputs plus the identity version
event_id.closed_field_inputs_note: The event identity is derived from exactly these inputs and the identity version. Adding, dropping or renaming an input is a new identity version, not a silent change.

canonicalization.note: event_id is sha256 over the utf8 of the JSON array [identity_version, then the closed_field_inputs values in order], serialized with no insignificant whitespace. The canonical bytes are fully determined by the pinned version and the pinned ordered inputs; no runtime implementation exists.

derivation.note: The host derives the event identity from the canonical inputs. A caller-supplied event id is forbidden and is rejected before persistence and before any read-back; a missing or false derivation requirement is a failure.

comparison.note: The read-back is accepted only when it echoes the exact event identity and the same confirmed field values. A read-back with a different or absent event_id is a failure, not a fuzzy match.

tested_source_revision.subject: prd/architecture/m210-s04-finding-evidence-matrix.json
tested_source_revision.meaning: live T02 matrix content digest carried on every review card
tested_source_revision.note: This is a content digest of one matrix artifact, not the whole-tree aggregate source revision.

reviewed_git_revision.subject: RC28 review packet reviewed revision
reviewed_git_revision.note: The packet reviewed revision and the future ledger event source_revision share the git40 namespace; neither is the card content digest.

revision_namespaces.no_fake_mapping_note: No function maps a sha256:64 content digest to a git40 commit or back. A claim that either namespace implies the other is a failure.

required_future_proof.note: A future submission binds both revisions to their own immutable inputs and to the confirmed card. A revision that resolves to no immutable input is unbound and fails.

drift_policy.action_on_drift: cancel the proposal, discard the read-back and require a new review

named_fail_closed.condition: an actor_class or actor_id supplied by the caller is treated as authority without a host-derived session binding
a submission claims host authority without a verified session identity, an authority epoch or operation-fenced references
a submission is applied while the actor-bound path is unavailable
a submission derives authority from a source on the forbidden list

submission_gate.limitation_note: The published review-case application validates a caller-supplied actor_class and actor_id only. That validation is not authentication. It is an inherited runtime weakness and a prerequisite for the future actor-bound scope, not something this design-only task repairs.

event_submission_delta_binding.note: The event submission delta binds to this contract by content digest and stays applied=false.

non_claims: This is a design-only session contract. It creates no event, writes no ledger, selects no option and records no disposition.
A recommendation stays advisory; accepting the contract is not accepting any finding.
Variant C acceptance through S02 subjective-UAT is not authority for record_human_disposition and does not answer any finding.
The future event identity is a specification with closed inputs and a version; no event with that identity exists.
The future event identity is host-derived and verified against the canonical inputs before persistence and read-back; a caller-supplied event id is forbidden.
The tested_source_revision content digest and the reviewed_git_revision commit are different namespaces and neither may be substituted for the other.
The submission gate stays applied=false until a host-controlled actor-bound path with a verified session identity exists.
No requirement is promoted and RC28 stays on hold until valid per-finding dispositions exist through the actor-bound path.
